Record 56,209,000 Women Not In Labor Force

The month of July also saw a record 93,770,000 Americans not participating in the labor force. This does not bode well for our economy. We need to seriously turn things around if we want to see improvements to the quality of life of Americans.
Quality of life is pretty damned good if you are a politically connected, crony capitalist living out in the Hamptons, so at least we gat that going for us...

This is a complex issue with many factors that people should be aware of. Some of these factors bode poorly for the future of the US economy.

  1. Many women (and men) just don't have skills that are needed. So they only qualify for low-paying jobs. Women with children often have to pay for child care. When you pay for child care you might net only $100-200 per month, and from that you have to pay all your bills. It's simply cheaper to go on welfare. "Welfare pays more than entry-level jobs in 35 states". Can you blame them for wanting welfare? Critics have noticed some issues with this study, issues which are relatively minor, but the point of the study is this: the welfare system, and the economy, is still broken. Just because Wall Street has recovered does not mean the average working Joan has.
  2. The job market is tight still. 99% of companies in the US have 500 or fewer employees, that means they are classified as "small business". Many are still desperately trying to make ends meet. Recent Obamacare regulations that went into effect over the past 3 years mean they have to cut hours for many of the lowest paid hourly employees to a max of 29 hours per week on average. (I'm the guy that calculates the average weekly hours so they don't go over.) Because if they got an average of 30 hours a week or more the company must provide them the same healthcare insurance as the rest of the people get. Small business simply can't afford this. So when employment is calculated by the feds, most of these low-wage people have 2 part time jobs, not one full time job, and often have no insurance, because it's cheaper to pay the Obamafine. They simply cannot afford healthcare after all of Obama's promises.
  3. College is still too costly for people to get better skills, and graduates from "tech" schools like DeVry and ITT Tech have a job placement rate of about 10-20%. It's much worse than you think it is. (Per news story earlier this year.)

Interesting points. I’ll offer my perspectives on them.

  1. Many people don’t have the skills that are needed - This is one I hear a lot, and while being accurate, it doesn’t research the very people themselves. Were these the same people who failed to take their education even remotely seriously as a child? Were they too busy being “cool” to concern themselves with the STEM fields? I would wager that these folks didn’t care about their education when they were young, and didn’t care about furthering their education when they got older. This is not something that I can feel sorry for them about. While I’m sure there are examples of good kids growing up and just not finding any opportunities, they are likely not in the majority. Go to any high school these days and see it unfolding right before your eyes. As for the solution, I’ll discuss that in #4.

  2. Daycare - This is a significant factor for a lot of people. While I take the position that people are having far too many kids to begin with, and most probably shouldn’t breed until they have their lives put together, there are still those cases where quality daycare could dramatically improve ones standing. There are a variety of factors contributing to this problem. The first is lawsuits. Americans, idiots that we are, are sue-happy. Spill coffee on yourself like an imbecile and you can sue and get a couple million (that isn’t taxed by the way). This problem spreads into daycare. They have to have expensive insurance to cover absolutely anything that can happen. Murphy’s Law doesn’t give a shit if you run a daycare or not. Figure out a way to stop the lawsuits and you’re well on your way to affordable child care. Next is the facility and the personnel. You want a good facility, and you certainly want quality personnel there. The facilities aren’t cheap because of the property tax fiasco in this nation where it always goes up and it gets more and more expensive to own land. These businesses can’t run without paying their bills. Same goes for the quality people. You’re going to want to screen the hell out of them and make damn sure only the best work there to make sure you don’t find yourself on the news. Paying people quality wages for their quality service will cost you. My solution to this is to give all daycare facilities meeting rigorous standards tax exemption. If they can give those folks who believe there’s an invisible man in the sky tax exemption, we can certainly tax exempt child care. Second, hire retirees. These are the grandmas and grandpas of the area and they have a lot of free time, are generally well educated, and also fill the role of “elder”. They like interaction, and they are knowledgeable. They also have no problem not pulling a 40 hour shift. As for the facilities. Think of all the quality buildings that are in bankruptcy right now. There’s our opportunity. There’s a local example of this in Tacoma, Washington. A hotel was going bankrupt and the state bought it from them for a steal. It’s now, Stadium High School in Tacoma. Google it. These facilities can be acquired, be run tax free, by retirees, with new stipulations that prohibit lawsuits. Problem solved.

  3. The job market is tight - perhaps where you live. Here in the Pacific Northwest, we’re going strong. There are lots of help wanted signs up, and people are taking those jobs. Is it perfect? No. I doubt there’ll ever be an example of “perfect”. The Obamacare thing is something that hit this nation hard, and lots of people are suffering for it now. Problem is, healthcare could be affordable to everyone if we sue-happy folks would stop the lawsuits. Second of all, we need to change the medical field in the US from being a for profit industry, to being a tax exempt non-profit system. The personnel still get paid well, but we need to get big business out of it. When it comes to business, they’ll cut absolutely every corner they can to improve their bottom line. They don’t care about the people, they care about their share holders. The solution to this is to remove the shareholders entirely, and to remove the required profit they need to show those shareholders. Watch the prices come crashing down. Suddenly, things are affordable. Best yet, the personnel still get paid well so it remains a desirable field.

  4. College is still too costly - I think most Americans are idiots when it comes to pursuing a degree to begin with. What’s the point? To show some dipshit in HR that you can stick with something for four to six years and have the will to go massively in debt for the privilege? It’s ridiculous. Want to solve the problem? How about we tell the businesses in the US that instead of degrees, how about you take people in and teach them to do exactly what you want them to do? It’d be a whole hell of a lot faster, and you’d have people training the new workers exactly the way you want them. Degrees mean nothing in most cases. If you’re going to be a surgeon, fine. If you’re going to be an industrial worker, just get to the job site and the guys on the job could teach you more in four hours than college would ever teach you. On the Job Training is where it’s at, and this country’s obsession with degrees for degree’s-sake will contribute to it’s downfall. Of course, it goes back to who’s profiting? The schools certainly are. The people issuing the student loans certainly are. All at the expense of the businesses that receive these graduates and have to train them once they get there anyway. Bypass all of that college bullshit and start up a tax break system in this nation where companies get a tax break when providing OJT to people, and they must have at least 35 hours a week. No more of this 29 hours per week shit.
